try-with-resources-basics.title: Try-with-resources
try-with-resources-basics.why: Resources declared in the try header are closed automatically even when the body throws.
try-with-resources-basics.tips: Prefer it to manual finally blocks for streams, readers, writers, and other AutoCloseable objects.

optional-or-else-get.title: Lazy Optional fallback
optional-or-else-get.short: Compute a fallback only when needed
optional-or-else-get.summary: Use orElseGet when producing the fallback is nontrivial.
optional-or-else-get.why: orElseGet invokes its supplier only when the Optional is empty.
optional-or-else-get.tips: Use orElse for cheap constants and orElseGet for work with side effects or meaningful cost.

list-copy-of.title: Immutable list snapshot
list-copy-of.short: Copy elements into an unmodifiable list
list-copy-of.summary: Use List.copyOf to make an unmodifiable snapshot-like list.
list-copy-of.why: List.copyOf clearly expresses that callers should not mutate the resulting list.
list-copy-of.tips: Elements themselves are not deep-copied, and null elements are rejected.

files-read-string.title: Read a file as a String
files-read-string.short: Use Files.readString for small text files
files-read-string.summary: Read all text from a path with an explicit charset.
files-read-string.why: Files.readString avoids manual reader loops when the entire text reasonably fits in memory.
files-read-string.tips: For very large files, stream or process lines instead of loading everything at once.

unsupported-operation-unmodifiable-list.title: Mutating an unmodifiable list
unsupported-operation-unmodifiable-list.summary: Do not call mutating List operations on an unmodifiable result.
unsupported-operation-unmodifiable-list.why: Factories such as List.copyOf return lists whose mutating methods throw UnsupportedOperationException.
unsupported-operation-unmodifiable-list.tips: Create an ArrayList copy when a mutable working collection is required.

integer-parse-overflow.title: Integer parsing outside int range
integer-parse-overflow.short: Text can be numeric but still too large for int
integer-parse-overflow.summary: Choose a numeric type whose range can contain the parsed value.
integer-parse-overflow.why: Integer.parseInt throws NumberFormatException when the value represented by valid digits lies outside int range.
integer-parse-overflow.tips: Use long or BigInteger when the input domain can exceed int limits.

switch-expression-missing-yield.title: Missing yield in a switch expression block
switch-expression-missing-yield.short: A switch expression block must produce a value
switch-expression-missing-yield.summary: Use yield when a block arm of a switch expression returns its result.
switch-expression-missing-yield.why: A block used as a switch expression arm cannot produce its value with a bare expression statement.
switch-expression-missing-yield.tips: Use the arrow expression form when no statements are needed before the value.

record-cannot-extend-class.title: A record cannot extend a class
record-cannot-extend-class.short: Records already have a fixed superclass
record-cannot-extend-class.summary: Use interfaces rather than a custom superclass for record polymorphism.
record-cannot-extend-class.why: Every record implicitly extends java.lang.Record, so Java does not allow another extends clause.
record-cannot-extend-class.tips: If shared implementation through inheritance is required, a normal class may be the better model.

rawtypes-list-warning.title: Raw List warning
rawtypes-list-warning.short: Keep generic type arguments instead of using raw collections
rawtypes-list-warning.summary: Parameterize collection types so the compiler can check element types.
rawtypes-list-warning.why: A raw List discards generic type information and can allow unsafe operations that surface later as casts or failures.
rawtypes-list-warning.tips: Use List<T> and the diamond operator unless interoperating with genuinely legacy raw APIs.

optional-or-else-eager.title: Optional.orElse evaluates eagerly
optional-or-else-eager.short: The fallback expression runs even when a value is present
optional-or-else-eager.summary: Use orElseGet when fallback creation should happen only for an empty Optional.
optional-or-else-eager.why: Java evaluates method arguments before the call, so the expression passed to orElse runs regardless of Optional presence.
optional-or-else-eager.tips: This matters when the fallback is expensive, changes state, performs I/O, or logs.
